newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen buying 76,000t corn, 10,000t soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen buying 76,000t corn, 10,000t soybeans.

text.p: Taiwanese buyers are expected to tender for at least 76,000 tonnes of U.S. corn -- more if prices fall -- and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans this week, local traders said on Monday.
Members Feed Industry Group was seen purchasing 56,000 tonnes U.S. No.2 corn for delivery in early October from the U.S. Gulf, or late October from the Pacific Northwest, they said.

State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp said it would tender soon for a combined shipment of 20,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soybeans for delivery from September 20 to October 5 from the U.S. Gulf or October 5-20 from the Pacific Northwest.

But Taiwan is not seen entering the international wheat market near term after the Flour Mills Association and the Provincial Food Bureau bought a total of 113,470 tonnes of U.S. wheat at tenders last week.
Association official Lu Wei-chih said current wheat supplies should last about two months.
Wheat flour was quoted at between T$14.55 to T$15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.
Soymeal was indicated at T$9.4 to T$9.5 for Taipei delivery down from between T$9.50 to T$9.70 a week previously.
Corn powder was priced at between T$7.05 to T$7.10 a kg for Taipei delivery, down from T$7.18.

Freight rates to Taiwan from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were quoted at about US$10.50 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico at between $20.35-$21 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized November and December shipments.
